(paratrag.). (With ὑπό (ὕπο) cf. Skt. úpa 'towards, near to, etc.', Goth. uf 'under'.) WITH GENITIVE, of Place, with Verbs of motion, from under, αὖτις ἀναστήσονται ὑ. ζόφου they will rise again from under the gloom,

(lyr.); αἰ μήτις αὐτὸς δοίη, μὴ ὑπ' ἀνάγκας not under compulsion,
(Vaxos). ὑπό freq. serves to denote the attendant or accompanying circumstances,
νέφος ἐρχόμενον κατὰ πόντον ὑ. Ζεφύροιο ἰωῆς Il. 4.276
, etc.: sts. with part. added, ἀμφὶ δὲ νῆες σμερδαλέον κονάβησαν ἀϋσάντων ὑπ' Ἀχαιῶν at their shouting, i.e. when they shouted,
ἴαχε σάλπιγξ ἄστυ περιπλομένων δηΐων ὕ. 18.220

. POSITION: ὑ. can follow its Subst., becoming by anastrophe ὕπο. It is freq. separated from the Subst. by intervening words, as in
:—ὑπαί is placed after its case in
, Inach. l.c., although acc. to Hdn.Gr.
it cannot suffer anastrophe. AS ADV., under, below, beneath, freq. in
; esp. of young animals, under the mother, i.e. at the breast,
. ὑπ' ἐκ or ὑπέκ, v. ὑπέκ. —In
the separation of the Prep. from its Verb by tmesis is very freq., and sts. it follows, in which case it suffers anastrophe,

. IN COMPOSITION: under, as well of rest as of motion, as in ὕπειμι, ὑποβαίνω, etc. of the casing or covering of one thing with another, as ὑπάργυρος, ὑπόχρυσος. of the agency or influence under which a thing is done, to express subjection or subordination, ὑποδαμνάω, ὑποδμώς, ὑφηνίοχος, cf. ἐπί G.
. denoting what is in small degree or gradual, somewhat, a little, as in ὑποκινέω, ὑποδεής, ὑπόλευκος (so in tmesi,
ὑ. τι μικρὸν ἐπιθήκισα Ar. V. 1290
(lyr.)). underhand, secretly, as in ὑποθέω, ὑποθωπεύω, ὑποκορίζομαι, ὑπόρνυμι.
